title: Income statement
summary: Revenue minus costs for the month: how much the business earns before and after income tax.

what: The income statement organizes the revenue and expenses of a period to show how much the business earns (or loses).
Gross sales include taxes; the cost of sales comes from the cost of goods consumed; operating costs gather staff, the month's expenses and taxes on sales.
formula: Cost of sales = food cost + beverage cost
Operating costs = salaries + payroll charges + rent + utilities + general expenses + amortization + taxes + fees
Result before income tax = revenue − cost of sales − operating costs
Net result = result before income tax − income tax (35%)

variables.name: Gross sales
variables.description: Food and beverage revenue, taxes included.

variables.name: Cost of sales
variables.description: The cost of goods consumed (food and beverages).

variables.name: Operating costs
variables.description: The month's fixed costs plus taxes on sales.

variables.name: Income tax
variables.description: Applies only when the result is positive.

steps: Subtract cost of sales and operating costs from sales.
Work out the income tax and subtract it.

examples.title: Handbook statement
paragraphs: Operating costs: $537,577, including $223,600 of taxes on sales (20% of gross sales).
Result before income tax: $310,423. Tax (35%): $108,648.05. Net result: $201,774.95.

notes.text: If 24.5% of taxes is applied on net sales, gross sales must be reduced by about 20% to get back to net sales (1 − 1 ÷ 1.245 ≈ 19.7%).
The statement's fixed costs (operating costs without taxes on sales) are the ones used for the break-even point: $313,977 in the example.

sales-taxes.label: Taxes on sales
sales-taxes.placeholder: VAT, gross income tax and other taxes for the period (e.g. 223600)

steps.operating-costs: Operating costs = fixed costs + taxes on sales = {fixedCosts} + {salesTaxes} = {operatingCosts}
steps.result-before-income-tax: Result before income tax = revenue − cost of sales − operating costs = {totalSales} − {costOfSales} − {operatingCosts} = {resultBeforeIncomeTax}
